title: Node, Resource and Capability Identity
summary: Placement identity is layered: allocator nodeId, provider resource identity, network endpoint and capability generation are distinct evidence.
why: A route can remain semantically meaningful while a target incarnation or capability generation changes; the latter must invalidate stale placement assumptions.
invariants: The stable allocator nodeId is separate from provider resource identity and network endpoint.
Installed capability facts remain distinct from expiring capacity observations.
Managed execution must bind the exact placement target and current capability generation; copied target fields are not proof.
evidence_note: Grounded in Managed Node Host Profile semantics, Job-to-Node lease verification, and RexxOS Managed Compute MU v0.1-dev2 target-generation checks.
